Mutation testing distinguishes detection failures from mutants that cannot meaningfully test the detector. Equivalent mutants preserve behavior; invalid mutants cannot execute. Stryker excludes invalid mutants from its mutation-score denominator, while equivalence research supports excluding proven equivalent mutants. For data pipelines, the practical implication is to define applicability before execution, verify that each injection actually changes the intended data property, and report invalid, inapplicable, equivalent, and unresolved cases separately. Do not declare a surviving mutant equivalent merely because the detector missed it. ([Stryker metrics](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/mutation-testing-elements/mutant-states-and-metrics/), [equivalent-mutant research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09241))

DeepMutation establishes training-data and training-program mutations as useful fault injections, but detector evaluation requires independent evidence that corruption occurred. A suitable protocol records original values, changed records, operator preconditions, and expected violated invariants outside the detector. Measure detection coverage as detected verified corruptions divided by applicable, valid, non-equivalent injected corruptions; retain excluded-case counts and reasons. This protocol is a synthesis of mutation-testing principles, rather than a standardized data-pipeline metric. ([DeepMutation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.05206))

Pair corrupted cases with unchanged clean controls and verified harmless transformations. Report clean-control false-positive rate separately from corruption recall, preferably by operator and severity; use independently verified clean labels because unchanged data may already contain errors. Model disagreement alone is not a correctness oracle. Cleanlab requires out-of-sample predictions for label-error detection, and benchmark-label research validates suspected errors through human review—supporting independent adjudication rather than treating detector outputs as ground truth. ([Cleanlab documentation](https://docs.cleanlab.ai/v2.1.0/), [label-error study](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/f2217062e9a397a1dca429e7d70bc6ca-Paper-round1.pdf))
